# `silk/bench/view`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Says how the results of a benchmark suite should be shown: a kind of chart and the fields it
maps.

## When to use
Add a [`View`](#View) to a suite with `silk.bench.suite.Suite.view` when the default presentation
is not the one a reader needs: a line against an input size, a comparison against another
implementation than the reference, every sample of a noisy benchmark, or a chart of your
own kind.

## Details
A view holds no numbers and no code. It names a kind and sets fields, and the report
resolves it into a `silk.bench.record.Chart` with every number computed, which the
renderers only draw.

| Kind | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `table` | One value for each benchmark and implementation |
| `ratio` | Values relative to the reference, with interval whiskers |
| `bars` | Absolute values with whiskers |
| `distribution` | Every sample, warm-up runs dimmed |
| `line` | A value against a parameter of the suite |
| `percentiles` | A value against the percentile of the samples |
| `history` | A value against the recorded runs of the suite |
| `x-<name>` | Anything: the built-in renderers show it as a table |

The fields are the same for every kind, and a kind ignores the ones that mean nothing to it:

| Field | Value | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `y` | The unit to show, such as `ns/op`. A command suite has `ns`, `user-ns`, `sys-ns` and `peak-B` | The unit of the tables |
| `x` | What runs along the axis: `benchmark`, `name`, `impl`, or a parameter | `benchmark`; the parameter of a `line` |
| `series` | What each line or bar group is: the same choices as `x` | `impl` |
| `facet` | What each separate chart is | Whatever `x` and `series` leave |
| `stat` | `median`, `min`, `max`, `mean`, or a percentile such as `p99` | `median` |
| `error` | `interval` (the 95% interval of the median), `range`, or `none` | `interval` |
| `scale` | `linear`, `log` (the value axis), or `log-log` (both axes) | `linear` |
| `zero` | `true` to start the value axis at zero, `false` to fit the values | `true` |
| `normalize` | An implementation to divide every value by | The reference in a `ratio` |
| `sort` | `value` or `-value` to order the entries of `x` by their first series | The order they ran in |
| `title` | The heading | Written from the kind and the fields |

A view has a text form, [`View.text`](#View.impl.text), which is one line: the kind, then `field=value`
pairs. A program that prints result lines may print `view: line x=size y=ns/op` to suggest
a view; the views a suite declares win over the ones its programs suggest.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.view { View }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

// A view written in the tasks program is the same as the line a program prints.
effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut view = run View.line("size")
  run view.y("ns/op")
  run view.logLog()
  let text = run view.text()
  if text.view() != "line x=size y=ns/op scale=log-log" {
    return 1
  }
  let read = run View.parse("line x=size y=ns/op scale=log-log")
  let again = run read.text()
  if again.view() != text.view() {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 3
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `View` with `import silk.bench.view { View }`.

## `View`

```silk
pub struct View
```

A presentation of the results of a suite: a kind of chart and the fields it maps.

### Details
The fields are public so a tool can read a view. Build one with the functions named after
the kinds, such as [`View.line`](#View.impl.line), and set fields with the methods below.

<a id="View.kind"></a>

### Field `kind`

```silk
pub kind: String
```

The kind, such as `line` or `x-flame`.

<a id="View.fields"></a>

### Field `fields`

```silk
pub fields: List<Pair>
```

The fields that were set, in the order they were first set.

like `table`, so name your own kinds `x-<name>`.

```silk
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a view that shows a value against the parameter `x` of the suite, such as an
input size or a thread count.

<a id="View.impl.percentiles"></a>

### Associated function `percentiles`

```silk
pub effect fn percentiles() -> View
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a view that shows a value against the percentile of the samples, as a load test
reads its latencies.

#### Details
When the result lines carry units such as `p50-ns` and `p99-ns` and the view's `y` is
`ns`, the chart shows what the lines report. Otherwise the percentiles are taken from the
samples of `y`.

<a id="View.impl.history"></a>

### Associated function `history`

```silk
pub effect fn history() -> View
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a view that shows a value against the recorded runs of the suite, with the run
being reported last.

<a id="View.impl.custom"></a>

### Associated function `custom`

```silk
pub effect fn custom(name: string) -> View
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a view of the kind `x-<name>`, for a renderer of your own. The report resolves it
like `table` and carries every field through, also the ones it does not know.

<a id="View.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(text: string) -> View
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the view that `text` describes: a kind, then `field=value` pairs separated by
spaces. A value with spaces is written in double quotes, with `\"` for a quote inside it.
Text without a kind gives a `table`.
